bullets.title: NVDA/Semis: Tech-led selloff as Samsung miss, DeepSeek chip fears trigger momentum unwind
bullets.body: Samsung Q2 revenue missed consensus by 0.7% (KRW171T), triggering a global momentum selloff in semis. China's DeepSeek developing its own AI chips to reduce Nvidia/Huawei reliance added to pressure. JPM notes NVDA is 'Central Bank of AI' via neocloud backstop agreements but flagged $7T debt expected by 2029 in AI financing as a structural concern; Mag7 trading near trough levels vs SPX while semis valuations remain elevated.

bullets.title: META: +2.6% on Muse Image launch from Superintelligence Labs; Erste upgrades to Buy
bullets.body: Meta launched Muse Image, its first generative AI image model from Superintelligence Labs, rolling out across Meta AI, Instagram, and WhatsApp with advertiser integration via Advantage+. Stock gained ~$17 to $617. Erste Group upgraded META to Buy citing the model launch.

bullets.title: MSFT: Replacing OpenAI/Anthropic with in-house models in Excel and Outlook
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Microsoft is deploying its own AI models in Excel and Outlook, replacing OpenAI and Anthropic partnerships in certain products as a cost-cutting measure. This signals accelerating AI capability consolidation internally at Microsoft.

bullets.title: SHOP: BofA reinstates Buy at $150 PT (21% upside)
bullets.body: BofA's Tal Liani reinstated Shopify at Buy with a $150 price target, implying ~21% upside from $124.06. Stock also trading up 3.1% on the TSX intraday.

bullets.title: ADBE: BofA reinstates at Underperform, $190 PT (16% downside)
bullets.body: BofA's Tal Liani reinstated Adobe at Underperform with a $190 price target, implying approximately 16% downside from $225.57.

bullets.title: TSLA: JPM analyzes SpaceX-Tesla combination — strategically coherent but regulatory risk is gating item
bullets.body: JPM views a SPCX-TSLA combination as strategically coherent, unifying AI, robotics, energy, transportation, and space under Musk with ~$28.5T TAM. However, regulatory scrutiny is the gating item: SPCX's defense/government contracts, TSLA's China manufacturing footprint, and governance asymmetry (Musk controls ~85% SPCX voting vs ~20% TSLA) complicate any deal. SPCX's ~$2.2T market cap exceeds TSLA's $1.4T, implying SPCX acquisition of TSLA; an all-stock SPCX-led acquisition is viewed as the most likely structure.

bullets.title: NET: Upgraded to sector outperform; cybersecurity spend rising with frontier AI
bullets.body: Cloudflare was upgraded to sector outperform, cited as a beneficiary of rising cybersecurity spend driven by frontier AI model adoption.

bullets.title: AMZN: $25B bond sale; $200B capex guided for 2026; hyperscaler demand recovery noted
bullets.body: Amazon is planning a $25B eight-part bond sale — the debt issuance is weighing on hyperscaler bonds as traders sell existing securities. AMZN guided for $200B capex in 2026 vs $131B in 2025. JPM notes hyperscaler demand recovery (GOOGL, AMZN) as sentiment rebounds from prior negative tone.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS Buy, $275 PT; Google Cloud agentic AI partnership targets mid-market
bullets.body: UBS maintains Buy on Accenture with a $275 PT (16x 2028E EPS). Accenture and Google Cloud launched agentic AI solutions via Accenture Edge targeting $300M–$3B revenue companies, integrating Gemini Enterprise and Agentic Data Cloud. Cybersecurity business grew from ~$700M in 2016 to $10B in 2025 (35% CAGR); OT security acquisitions (Dragos, runZero, NetRise) could triple addressable market.

bullets.title: AI Capex Air Pocket: demand arriving in separate waves, monetization timing mismatch flagged
bullets.body: A research note identifies three divergent AI demand curves — coding inference (accelerating), enterprise AI (constrained by governance/privacy), and consumer personal assistants (slower than expected). Meta acknowledged agentic AI progress slower than expected and is building a cloud business to sell excess compute. The note flags an 'air pocket' risk as investors priced a synchronized adoption cycle; market is shifting from rewarding AI capex by default to demanding measurable ROI and revenue conversion clarity. Relevant to META, GOOGL, AMZN, AAPL, MSFT, PLTR, NVDA.

bullets.title: FSLR: Deutsche Bank upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $272 from $245
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank upgraded First Solar to Buy and raised its price target to $272 from $245, citing a stronger H2 outlook, normalized 2027, and expected tariff policy clarifications. The recent pullback is viewed as a buying opportunity. Broader renewables sector was sharply lower today (OKLO -7.7%, BE -8.7%, SMR -6.9%).

bullets.title: CZR: Jefferies shopping ~$5B debt for Carl Icahn rival bid ahead of 7/11 go-shop deadline
bullets.body: Jefferies is approaching investors/creditors to raise ~$5B in debt to support Carl Icahn's potential competing bid for Caesars Entertainment. Caesars agreed to a Fertitta acquisition at $31/share (~$17.6B including debt) on May 28; the go-shop period expires July 11.

bullets.title: FWONK: JPM Overweight; strong sponsorship pricing power, 4x licensing upside, Vegas extended to 2037
bullets.body: JPM maintains Overweight on Liberty Formula One following management meetings. Sponsorship pricing power is accelerating, with official partners now paying what global partners paid years ago. Licensing revenue has 4x uplift potential. Las Vegas race extended to 2037 with ticket sales pacing ahead of 2025. Germany media rights (expiring after 2027) represent the largest upcoming renewal with Netflix, Prime Video, and Disney+ expected to bid.

bullets.title: ETSY: MS stays Equal Weight; purchase intent at -10%, alt data disconnect raises yellow flag
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Equal Weight on ETSY after June survey showed N3M net purchase intent at -10% (vs -18% in April), remaining among the lowest surveyed. Weakness concentrated in $50K-$100K HHI cohort; strong alt data contradicts weak intent, raising a caution flag post re-rating. EBAY remains MS's preferred name in SMID eCommerce (OW) with purchase intent at -1%, near-record reading, and GMV growth accelerating from ~3% in 1H25 to ~12% in 1H26.

bullets.title: PENN/BYD/CZR: Ohio racino 2Q GGR beats estimates; BYD +21.5%, PENN +7.1%
bullets.body: Ohio 2Q racino GGR came in at +6.3% YoY vs. estimates of ~+2-6%. BYD's Belterra Park was the standout at +21.5% YoY vs. a +2% estimate. PENN's racino properties delivered +7.1% vs. +3% estimate; CZR's Scioto Downs +8.3% vs. +6% estimate.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Data center REITs +1.75% daily, +25.68% YTD; AI warehouse demand cited
bullets.body: Data Center REITs outperformed the broader market (S&P RE Index +1.6% vs S&P 500 -0.45%) driven by AI-related warehouse demand. Tech giants (Meta, Google) leasing ~4MSF warehouse space in 2026 for data center support; JLL projects 14MSF by 2030.

bullets.title: TMUS: Public Storage COO Chris Sambar departs to join T-Mobile as Chief Enterprise Officer
bullets.body: Chris Sambar, COO of Public Storage, resigned effective end of July 2026 to become T-Mobile's Chief Enterprise Officer. Operations leadership will report directly to CEO Tom Boyle until a permanent replacement is named.

bullets.title: TSM: Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight on TSMC foundry dominance
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterated its Overweight rating on TSMC, citing the company's continued dominance in leading-edge foundry amid the broader semiconductor selloff.

bullets.title: Price Momentum factor worst week since 2022; semis/hardware longs vs. software shorts the core unwind
bullets.body: The price momentum factor (CIISPMUT) fell 6.6% w/w, the 2nd worst 5-day pullback since 2004, driven by the unwind of long semis/tech hardware vs. short software positioning. EPS Momentum remains resilient at -1.8% from peak. Historically, momentum bounces ~70% of the time after sharp drawdowns; earnings season may be the catalyst. Citi recommends QQQ puts and semis congestion as hedges; baseline remains bullish on AI capex durability.

bullets.title: SHOP/FIG/ADBE: BofA reinstates trio — Buy on SHOP ($150) and FIG ($30), Underperform on ADBE ($190)
bullets.body: BofA analyst Tal Liani reinstated coverage: SHOP Buy at $150 PT (~21% upside), FIG Buy at $30 PT (~29% upside from $23.24), and ADBE Underperform at $190 PT (~16% downside from $225.57).
